To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the liver volume (LV), which is the key factor in the determination of the minimum liver volume (MLV) necessary for a liver transplantation recipient, is estimated by using the body weight (BW) and body surface area (SA) in the adult population, but the estimation is not accurate for the children and the adults because the LV/BW or LV/SA is not constant with age or BW.

the liver density (LD) of Koreans (1.04 kg/L) is lower than that of Caucasians (1.06 kg/L), and that the standard liver volume (SLV) of Koreans (estimated as 21.585 BW 0.732 BH 0.225) is lower than those of Caucasians and Japanese (estimated as 25 BW 0.67 BH 0.25 and 24 BW 0.75 BH 0.23, respectively).
a better LV estimation formula for the Korean population was established as LV (mL)=21.585×BW(kg)0.732×BH(cm)0.225(adjusted R2=0.59;SE=275.8mL).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of liver volume in Korean population.
the standard liver volume (SLV) estimation for liver transplantation (LT) in the Korean population.
the estimation of standard liver volume (SLV) in Korean adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no simple linear relationship between liver volume and body surface area, but there is a strong relationship between liver volume (or weight) and body weight.
a simple linear formula is not suitable for the LV estimation in children or adults.
the Japanese formula produces an underestimate of the standard liver volume (SV) for the Korean population, whereas the Caucasian formula produces random errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a better LV estimation formula for the Korean population is as follows: LV (m L ) = 21.6 85 × BW (kg )0. 732 × BH ( cm )0.2 25 (adjusted R 2 = 0.59; SE =275.8 mL ).
the Japanese and Caucasian formulas for liver volume estimation are not appropriate for Korean population.
the standard liver volume for Korean population is 1.2-1.4 times of the body surface area.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a nonlinear or a piecewise linear formula may be better for liver volume estimation than a simple linear formula, because liver volume/body weight or liver volume/body surface area is not constant with age or body surface area.
the liver volume of a recipient is not simply proportional to the body weight or body surface area of the recipient.

there are differences between populations and that a standard liver volume formula that is derived in one population is not necessarily applicable to other populations, and this is especially true for pediatric recipients.
